symptoms.title: No supported disease pattern
symptoms.description: The image did not show a strong pattern for Black Sigatoka, Panama Disease, or Cordana Leaf Spot. This is not proof that the whole plant is disease-free.

symptoms.title: Inspect the whole plant
symptoms.description: Check both leaf surfaces, older and younger leaves, the pseudostem, and the plant base for yellowing, spots, wilting, splitting, or internal discoloration.

symptoms.title: Watch for changes
symptoms.description: Symptoms can be absent or subtle in an early infection. Compare the plant over time and scan a clear, well-lit image of any new symptom.

treatment.title: Do not apply a pesticide
treatment.description: A Healthy result does not require chemical treatment. Use a confirmed diagnosis before applying any pesticide.

treatment.title: Continue care suited to Sto. Tomas
treatment.description: Maintain balanced nutrition, good spacing, and drainage. Adjust watering after rainfall so the roots are not left waterlogged and the leaves do not remain wet unnecessarily.

treatment.title: Ask for help if symptoms continue
treatment.description: For continuing wilt, spreading spots, or internal discoloration, contact the Sto. Tomas City Agriculture Office at (043) 784-8022 local 307 or agri@cityofstotomas.gov.ph.

prevention.title: Inspect every week
prevention.description: Check both sides of older and younger leaves, the pseudostem, and the plant base, especially after several rainy or humid days.

prevention.title: Keep biosecurity clean
prevention.description: Use clean tools and footwear, avoid moving soil between plots, and obtain healthy planting material from a reliable source.

prevention.title: Prepare drainage before heavy rain
prevention.description: Keep canals and runoff paths clear, avoid waterlogging, and maintain airflow and suitable spacing around each mat.

prevention.title: Record changes
prevention.description: Photograph and rescan new symptoms in good light. Seek advice from the City Agriculture Office when symptoms persist or spread.
